Departure 1000 is the fifth item on p.55; p.56 opens with the word 出撃 (sortie) and ends with the arrival line, so I read them as one run. The first digit of the arrival time is a small circle and could be read 0230 (30 Aug) instead of 2330; 2330 fits the time order of that page and a run of about 13.5 h. No speed on these lines. Which ships the divisions held is not on these pages: 24th less Suzukaze and 11th less Murakumo is as written.

The 20th Division (carrying the 28 Aug landing) was bombed at about 1430 north of Santa Isabel, the landing was stopped and the force turned back; the 8th Fleet postponed the landing of the night of 28 Aug. Included to show that this run waited and manoeuvred near Santa Isabel, so do not use it as a transit. On p.52 an arrival at Shortland (0730, date unclear) of 24th Division (less Suzukaze) and Isokaze is entered; not used as an arrival because the day is not clear.

column25: Zone not stated; presumed Tokyo time. Clock is the document's own. Handwritten page read by me from the PDF image. Already recorded in the database as positions; this row joins them. The 200 nm in distance_nm_stated is the distance from Guadalcanal at sunset (1626), not the whole run. I re-read p.37 (departure 1200, 24 kn) and p.38 (24 kn, then 30 kn). Check by arithmetic (inferred): Shortland Harbour to Savo is about 265 nm on the database positions; 4 h at 24 kn (96 nm) plus 5.55 h at 30 kn (166 nm) is 262 nm, so the stated speeds and times close. Other sources give the departure as 1000 or 1400 (already in the database: ja-wikipedia, wikipedia-en); this report says 1200.. The 200 nm in the report is not the length of the run: it is the force's position at sunset (1626), bearing 310 degrees and 200 nm from Guadalcanal. That is an intermediate fix, 4 hours 26 minutes after leaving at 24 knots

column18: He decided to carry out his planned night attack, and at 1500 headed south at twenty-four knots to pass through Bougainville Strait at 1537 ... column20: Bates and Innis, Chapter VII (printed pp.77-78: "headed south at twenty-four knots", "1537") and Chapter IX p.106 ("exactly 0000 ... twenty-six knots"); OCR text of https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA003037/DTIC_ADA003037.pdf; page markers in the OCR are unreliable
column25: Zone not stated in the lines read. Times are in the clock the Japanese used (Bates gives them as written). No start position is given for 1500, so no distance or average speed can be worked out. Two statements inside Bates differ: the Signal Order No. 26 said speed 24 kn for the rush in ("Speed will be twenty-four knots at the time of the rush in"), while the narrative has the force going to 26 kn at 0000 and keeping 26 kn on course 150 at 0105. The OCR reads "1664" for the 1654 turn (arithmetic: not a possible time, so 1654 is my reading). The 24-kn run was at one speed from 1500 to 0000 by this account, but the force changed course several times and cleared the strait, so the row is marked not steady.. Start as the source gives it: Bougainville Strait approach (position not stated). End as the source gives it: 37 nm from the south entrance of Tulagi, bearing 140
